claim: Meningitis is a potentially life-threatening infection characterized by the inflammation of the leptomeningeal membranes.
source: Meningitis is a potentially life-threatening infection characterized by the inflammation of the leptomeningeal membranes.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about meningitis that represents established medical knowledge.

claim: Many different viral and bacterial pathogens can cause meningitis, with differences in mortality rates, risk of developing neurological sequelae, and treatment options.
source: Many different viral and bacterial pathogens can cause meningitis, with differences in mortality rates, risk of developing neurological sequelae, and treatment options.
evidence: This statement reflects established medical knowledge about meningitis etiology and outcomes.

claim: A drastic and pathogen-type specific influx of tissue-, cell-, and plasma proteins occurs in the CSF during meningitis.
source: The results revealed a drastic and pathogen-type specific influx of tissue-, cell-, and plasma proteins in the CSF, where, in particular, a large increase of neutrophil-derived proteins in the CSF correlated with acute bacterial meningitis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental proteomics data presented in the study.

claim: A large increase of neutrophil-derived proteins in the CSF correlates with acute bacterial meningitis.
source: The results revealed a drastic and pathogen-type specific influx of tissue-, cell-, and plasma proteins in the CSF, where, in particular, a large increase of neutrophil-derived proteins in the CSF correlated with acute bacterial meningitis.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data showing elevated neutrophil proteins in ABM samples.

claim: Both acute bacterial and viral meningitis result in marked reduction of brain-enriched proteins.
source: Additionally, both acute bacterial and viral meningitis result in marked reduction of brain-enriched proteins.
evidence: This finding is supported by the proteomics measurements showing decreased brain-associated proteins.

claim: An 18-protein panel of cell- and tissue-associated proteins is capable of classifying acute bacterial meningitis and viral meningitis.
source: Generation of a multiprotein LASSO regression model resulted in an 18-protein panel of cell- and tissue-associated proteins capable of classifying acute bacterial meningitis and viral meningitis.
evidence: This claim is based on the LASSO regression modeling results presented in the study.

claim: The 18-protein panel enables classification of tick-borne encephalitis with high sensitivity and specificity.
source: The same protein panel also enabled classification of tick-borne encephalitis, a subgroup of viral meningitis, with high sensitivity and specificity.
evidence: This is supported by the LASSO model performance data showing high AUROC for TBE classification.

claim: Meningitis has an estimated annual prevalence of 8.7 million cases globally.
source: Meningitis is a common condition with an estimated annual prevalence of 8.7 million cases globally (Kassebaum et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kassebaum et al., 2017.

claim: In the majority of cases, meningitis is caused by viruses, such as enteroviruses, and is associated with low mortality rates.
source: In the majority of cases, meningitis is caused by viruses, such as enteroviruses, and is associated with low mortality rates (Chadwick, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chadwick, 2005.

claim: Tick-borne encephalitis is associated with higher mortality rates and risk of developing neurological sequelae.
source: Certain subtypes of viral meningitis (VM), such as tick-borne encephalitis (TBE), are in contrast associated with higher mortality rates and risk of developing neurological sequelae (Bogovic and Strle, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bogovic and Strle, 2015.

claim: Acute bacterial meningitis is one of the leading causes of death due to infectious diseases worldwide.
source: Acute bacterial meningitis (ABM) is one of the leading causes of death due to infectious diseases worldwide and is associated with rapid disease progression, increased risk of long-term neurological sequelae in survivors, and high mortality rates (van de Beek et al., 2004; van de Beek et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to van de Beek et al., 2004 and 2006.

claim: Acute bacterial meningitis is associated with rapid disease progression, increased risk of long-term neurological sequelae in survivors, and high mortality rates.
source: Acute bacterial meningitis (ABM) is one of the leading causes of death due to infectious diseases worldwide and is associated with rapid disease progression, increased risk of long-term neurological sequelae in survivors, and high mortality rates (van de Beek et al., 2004; van de Beek et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to van de Beek et al., 2004 and 2006.

claim: Different bacterial and viral pathogens are associated with specific virulence mechanisms that impact the molecular phenotype of the host immune response.
source: The different bacterial and viral pathogens are associated with specific virulence mechanisms that impact the molecular phenotype of the host immune response.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about pathogen-host interactions.

claim: Diagnosis of meningitis routinely involves lumbar punctures to evaluate several parameters in the cerebrospinal fluid such as the number of white blood cells as well as glucose and protein concentrations to differentiate between ABM and VM.
source: This information can be used to diagnose patients with meningitis, which routinely involves lumbar punctures to evaluate several parameters in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) such as the number of white blood cells (WBCs) as well as glucose and protein concentrations to differentiate between ABM and VM (Ross et al., 1988).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ross et al., 1988.

claim: CSF parameters used for meningitis diagnosis are relatively non-specific yielding inconclusive diagnostic information.
source: Unfortunately, these parameters are relatively non-specific yielding inconclusive diagnostic information (Garty et al., 1997; Lindquist et al., 1988; Nigrovic et al., 2002), and it currently remains unknown if different pathogens and pathogen types can evoke detectable differences in host response proteome.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Garty et al., 1997; Lindquist et al., 1988; Nigrovic et al., 2002.

claim: It currently remains unknown if different pathogens and pathogen types can evoke detectable differences in host response proteome.
source: Unfortunately, these parameters are relatively non-specific yielding inconclusive diagnostic information (Garty et al., 1997; Lindquist et al., 1988; Nigrovic et al., 2002), and it currently remains unknown if different pathogens and pathogen types can evoke detectable differences in host response proteome.
evidence: This represents a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Extracellular body fluids such as blood plasma, saliva, and CSF are deficient in the machinery required for de novo protein synthesis.
source: Extracellular body fluids such as blood plasma, saliva, and CSF are deficient in the machinery required for de novo protein synthesis.
evidence: This represents established biological knowledge about body fluids.

claim: The protein constituents of body fluids are generated via active protein secretion from surrounding tissues or from passive leakage derived from normal protein turnover from cells and tissues.
source: The protein constituents of body fluids are generated via active protein secretion from surrounding tissues or from passive leakage derived from normal protein turnover from cells and tissues.
evidence: This represents established biological knowledge about protein composition of body fluids.

claim: During healthy conditions, the concentration of individual proteins in body fluids is maintained via a tightly controlled balance between protein secretion and clearance.
source: During healthy conditions, the concentration of individual proteins in body fluids is maintained via a tightly controlled balance between protein secretion and clearance.
evidence: This represents established biological knowledge about protein homeostasis.

claim: The balance between protein secretion and clearance is altered in severe infectious diseases such as sepsis or meningitis due to the host responses triggered by the invading pathogen.
source: This balance is altered in severe infectious diseases such as sepsis or meningitis due to the host responses triggered by the invading pathogen (Malmström et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Malmström et al., 2016.

claim: In meningitis and sepsis, the immune response normally increases cellular and acellular mediators in the CSF and plasma, which leads to a drastic proteome reorganization.
source: In meningitis and sepsis, the immune response normally increases cellular and acellular mediators in the CSF and plasma, which leads to a drastic proteome reorganization (Karlsson et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Karlsson et al., 2018.

claim: In the most severe stages of disease, host immune response becomes overwhelming, leading to organ damage and impaired prognosis.
source: In the most severe stages of disease, host immune response becomes overwhelming, leading to organ damage and impaired prognosis (van de Beek et al., 2004; van de Beek et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to van de Beek et al., 2004 and 2006.

claim: Detection of pathogen-specific host response patterns requires the analysis of large sample cohorts to compare host response patterns from a similar group of pathogens to all other pathogen types.
source: However, detection of pathogen-specific host response patterns requires the analysis of large sample cohorts to compare host response patterns from a similar group of pathogens to all other pathogen types.
evidence: This represents a methodological inference about study design requirements.

claim: As the protein composition of body fluids is produced elsewhere, mRNA transcript profiling is less suitable for the detection of host responses.
source: As the protein composition of body fluids is produced elsewhere, mRNA transcript profiling is less suitable for the detection of host responses.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the fact that body fluids lack protein synthesis machinery.

claim: Mass spectrometry-based protein quantification has become the preferred method for multiplexed and quantitative analysis of proteomes.
source: Mass spectrometry (MS)-based protein quantification has become the preferred method for multiplexed and quantitative analysis of proteomes (Aebersold and Mann, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Aebersold and Mann, 2016.

claim: The prevailing MS strategy relies on data-dependent acquisition (DDA), where the mass spectrometer sequentially selects and fragments trypsin-generated peptide ions to generate informative daughter fragment ion spectra used for database searching.
source: The prevailing MS strategy relies on data-dependent acquisition (DDA), where the mass spectrometer sequentially selects and fragments trypsin-generated peptide ions to generate informative daughter fragment ion spectra used for database searching.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about mass spectrometry methodology.

claim: DDA proteomics experiments enable identification of thousands of peptide ions.
source: Although such proteomics experiments enable identification of thousands of peptide ions, the strategy is associated with lower quantitative reproducibility, as in complex samples the number of available peptides exceeds the cycling time of the DDA method.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about DDA capabilities.

claim: DDA is associated with lower quantitative reproducibility because in complex samples the number of available peptides exceeds the cycling time of the DDA method.
source: Although such proteomics experiments enable identification of thousands of peptide ions, the strategy is associated with lower quantitative reproducibility, as in complex samples the number of available peptides exceeds the cycling time of the DDA method.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about DDA limitations.

claim: SWATH-MS generates fragment ion spectra of all MS-measurable peptides to produce a digital representation of the analyzed proteome.
source: In contrast, the recent development of sequential window acquisition of all theoretical fragment ion spectra (SWATH)-MS generates fragment ion spectra of all MS-measurable peptides to produce a digital representation of the analyzed proteome (Gillet et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gillet et al., 2012.

claim: In SWATH-MS, proteome maps are generated based on data-independent acquisition (DIA), followed by protein quantification using a priori established assay libraries.
source: In SWATH-MS, proteome maps are generated based on data-independent acquisition (DIA), followed by protein quantification using a priori established assay libraries (Teleman et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Teleman et al., 2017.

claim: Different assay libraries can be used to iteratively query the same DIA data in an iterative fashion.
source: Different assay libraries can be used to iteratively query the same DIA data in an iterative fashion, which is a considerable advantage as it permits a single data collection step for clinical samples (Guo et al., 2015) and focused reanalysis in future studies.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Guo et al., 2015.

claim: DIA is associated with a high degree of reproducibility, making it possible to merge data sets analyzed separately in time to perform cross-study comparisons.
source: Importantly, DIA is associated with a high degree of reproducibility, making it possible to merge data sets analyzed separately in time to perform cross-study comparisons.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about DIA methodology advantages.

claim: CSF was collected by lumbar puncture from a cohort of 135 patients admitted to the hospital with the suspicion of meningitis.
source: Here, CSF was collected by lumbar puncture from a cohort of 135 patients admitted to the hospital with the suspicion of meningitis.
evidence: This describes the experimental sample collection performed in the study.

claim: Following confirmed diagnosis, the patients were broadly subdivided into ABM (n = 35), neuroborreliosis (BM, n = 7), VM (n = 21), suspected ABM (n = 5), suspected VM (n = 16), and inflammation without infection (n = 2).
source: Following confirmed diagnosis, the patients were broadly subdivided into ABM (n = 35), neuroborreliosis (BM, n = 7), VM (n = 21), suspected ABM (n = 5), suspected VM (n = 16), and inflammation without infection (n = 2).
evidence: This describes the patient cohort classification in the study.

claim: In this cohort, ABM was caused by 11 different bacterial pathogens, where the most frequent pathogen was Streptococcus pneumoniae.
source: In this cohort, ABM was caused by 11 different bacterial pathogens, where the most frequent pathogen was Streptococcus pneumoniae.
evidence: This describes the pathogen distribution in the study cohort.

claim: VM was caused by seven different viruses with the highest frequency of TBE and enteroviruses.
source: VM was caused by seven different viruses with the highest frequency of TBE and enteroviruses (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the viral pathogen distribution shown in Figure 1.

claim: Patients with suspected meningitis but with normal WBC count (<5 × 106/L) and with no clinical signs of infection/inflammation were regarded as a control group (n = 49).
source: Patients with suspected meningitis but with normal WBC count (<5 × 106/L) and with no clinical signs of infection/inflammation were regarded as a control group (n = 49).
evidence: This describes the control group definition in the study.

claim: A total of 771 unique human proteins were confidently detected and quantified in this analysis.
source: A total of 771 unique human proteins were confidently detected and quantified in this analysis.
evidence: This is a direct result from the proteomics analysis.

claim: The sample group containing the largest number of unique proteins was ABM (n = 719 versus n = 544 in controls), followed by VM (n = 550) and BM (n = 478).
source: The sample group containing the largest number of unique proteins was ABM (n = 719 versus n = 544 in controls), followed by VM (n = 550) and BM (n = 478).
evidence: This is a direct result from the proteomics analysis.

claim: On average, the total protein intensities in ABM were 2, 2.7, and 4.3 times higher than in BM, VM, and the control group, respectively.
source: On average, the total protein intensities in ABM were 2, 2.7, and 4.3 times higher than in BM, VM, and the control group, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The majority of proteins detected are secreted (between 37% and 48% across all samples), followed by membrane-bound proteins, which comprised 18–24% of the total protein content.
source: Analysis of the subcellular compartment of the detected proteins revealed that the majority of proteins are secreted (between 37% and 48% across all samples), followed by membrane-bound proteins, which comprised 18–24% of the total protein content (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This is a result from subcellular compartment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a.

claim: The average intensity for the secreted proteins was 5.9-fold higher in ABM versus control and 2.7–2.9-fold higher in ABM when compared to BM or VM.
source: The average intensity for the secreted proteins was 5.9-fold higher in ABM versus control and 2.7–2.9-fold higher in ABM when compared to BM or VM (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Numerous neutrophil-, plasma-, and brain-associated proteins constitute on average 15–20% of the protein intensity.
source: We observe that numerous neutrophil-, plasma-, and brain-associated proteins constitute on average 15–20% of the protein intensity, where, in particular, the neutrophil proteins increased during ABM (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Neutrophil proteins increased during ABM.
source: We observe that numerous neutrophil-, plasma-, and brain-associated proteins constitute on average 15–20% of the protein intensity, where, in particular, the neutrophil proteins increased during ABM (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Plasma proteins are known to be major constituents of CSF under physiological conditions.
source: Plasma proteins are known to be major constituents of CSF under physiological conditions (Guldbrandsen et al., 2014), and presence of brain-associated proteins in CSF is likely related to protein turnover in the brain.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Guldbrandsen et al., 2014.

claim: Presence of brain-associated proteins in CSF is likely related to protein turnover in the brain.
source: Plasma proteins are known to be major constituents of CSF under physiological conditions (Guldbrandsen et al., 2014), and presence of brain-associated proteins in CSF is likely related to protein turnover in the brain.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed brain proteins in CSF.

claim: Statistical analysis between sample groups reveals 79 statistically induced or repressed proteins.
source: Statistical analysis between sample groups reveals 79 statistically induced or repressed proteins (Figure 2b–d).
evidence: This is a result from statistical analysis shown in Figure 2b–d.

claim: The majority of significantly altered proteins were associated with neutrophils (32% in ABM and 14% in VM), the brain (44% in ABM and 32% in VM), and some plasma proteins including several acute-phase proteins.
source: The majority of significantly altered proteins were associated with neutrophils (32% in ABM and 14% in VM), the brain (44% in ABM and 32% in VM), and some plasma proteins including several acute-phase proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 4a, b).
evidence: This is a result from tissue assignment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4a, b.

claim: Several neutrophil-associated proteins were induced ≥64-fold but not statistically significant, indicating a large degree of variation associated with these proteins.
source: In addition, several neutrophil-associated proteins were induced ≥64-fold (yellow dots) but not statistically significant, indicating a large degree of variation associated with these proteins.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of high fold-change but non-significant proteins.

claim: The average intensities of all neutrophil proteins show a significant increase only in ABM compared to controls.
source: For each group, the average intensities of all neutrophil proteins show a significant increase only in ABM compared to controls (Figure 2f), whereas there is a significant decrease in brain-associated proteins in ABM, VM, and TBE (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is a statistical result shown in Figure 2f.

claim: There is a significant decrease in brain-associated proteins in ABM, VM, and TBE.
source: For each group, the average intensities of all neutrophil proteins show a significant increase only in ABM compared to controls (Figure 2f), whereas there is a significant decrease in brain-associated proteins in ABM, VM, and TBE (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is a statistical result shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Among the gene ontology terms enriched for the repressed proteins in ABM was 'regulation of synapse maturation and assembly,' suggesting changes on the cellular level in neuronal circuits during ABM.
source: Among the gene ontology (GO) terms enriched for the repressed proteins in ABM was 'regulation of synapse maturation and assembly,' suggesting changes on the cellular level in neuronal circuits during ABM (Figure 2—figure supplement 4c).
evidence: This is an interpretation of GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4c.

claim: Notable GO terms for induced proteins in ABM were 'regulation of apoptotic signaling pathway,' 'defense response to bacterium,' and 'glial cell development.'
source: Of the induced proteins, notable GO terms were 'regulation of apoptotic signaling pathway,' 'defense response to bacterium,' and 'glial cell development.'
evidence: This is a result from GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The GO terms suggest increased apoptotic pathways and enriched molecular processes specialized in combating bacteria in the CSF of patients with ABM, followed by increased development of glial cells.
source: These suggest increased apoptotic pathways and enriched molecular processes specialized in combating bacteria in the CSF of patients with ABM, followed by increased development of glial cells, which are involved in maintaining chemical homeostasis and act as the immune cells of the CNS (Ransohoff and Brown, 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GO enrichment results, with citation support for glial cell function.

claim: Glial cells are involved in maintaining chemical homeostasis and act as the immune cells of the CNS.
source: These suggest increased apoptotic pathways and enriched molecular processes specialized in combating bacteria in the CSF of patients with ABM, followed by increased development of glial cells, which are involved in maintaining chemical homeostasis and act as the immune cells of the CNS (Ransohoff and Brown, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ransohoff and Brown, 2012.

claim: ABM and VM evoke a more similar response compared to BM.
source: This cross-comparison reveals that ABM and VM evoke a more similar response compared to BM.
evidence: This is an inference from the cross-comparison analysis of differentially expressed proteins.

claim: ABM was associated with 49 unique statistically significant proteins and VM 10 proteins and 16 proteins were shared between the disease groups.
source: In total, ABM was associated with 49 unique statistically significant proteins and VM 10 proteins and 16 proteins were shared between the disease groups (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a result from the Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Only three proteins, chitinase-3-like protein 2 (CHI3L2), immunoglobulin mu heavy chain disease protein (MUCB), and profilin-1 (PROF1), were found at higher levels in all the three diseased groups compared to control.
source: Only three proteins, chitinase-3-like protein 2 (CHI3L2), immunoglobulin mu heavy chain disease protein (MUCB), and profilin-1 (PROF1), were found at higher levels in all the three diseased groups compared to control (Figure 3e), although the intensities for these proteins are substantially higher in the ABM samples.

claim: The intensities for CHI3L2, MUCB, and PROF1 are substantially higher in the ABM samples.
source: Only three proteins, chitinase-3-like protein 2 (CHI3L2), immunoglobulin mu heavy chain disease protein (MUCB), and profilin-1 (PROF1), were found at higher levels in all the three diseased groups compared to control (Figure 3e), although the intensities for these proteins are substantially higher in the ABM samples.

source: Previous studies have shown an association between these proteins and neurological disease (Møllgaard et al., 2016; Narayanan et al., 2016; Opsahl et al., 2016).

claim: Neutrophil proteins are distinctive for ABM, but not for VM.
source: We observed that neutrophil proteins are distinctive for ABM, but not for VM.

claim: ABM led to increased levels of acute-phase proteins such as serum amyloid a-1 (SAA1) and C-reactive protein (CRP).
source: In addition, ABM also led to increased levels of acute-phase proteins such as serum amyloid a-1 (SAA1) and C-reactive protein (CRP).

claim: VM resulted in increased concentrations of C4b-binding protein and C-X-C motif chemokine 10 (CXCL10).
source: In contrast, VM resulted in increased concentrations of C4b-binding protein and C-X-C motif chemokine 10 (CXCL10), where the latter chemokine is elevated in plasma during viral infections.

claim: CXCL10 is elevated in plasma during viral infections.
source: In contrast, VM resulted in increased concentrations of C4b-binding protein and C-X-C motif chemokine 10 (CXCL10), where the latter chemokine is elevated in plasma during viral infections.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about CXCL10 in viral infections.

claim: Two of the tested groups had an AUROC above 0.90.

source: The protein profiles for ABM and control were reproducible across the 100 runs and specific, with a mean AUROC of 0.96 for ABM and 0.95 for controls.

source: TBE displayed the most stable and discriminatory AUROC of 0.87 of all specific causative-agent subgroups, indicating that TBE evokes a distinct host response.

source: In total, 18 proteins were detected in ≥90% of the 100 runs in every fold and had a nonzero weight, which were consistently used in the LASSO models for discriminating different sample groups.

source: 5 of the 18 proteins were in general detected in higher amounts in ABM and BM and include proteins such as gelsolin (GEL), cathepsin D (CATD), and transthyretin (TTHY) that are involved in neutrophil degranulation according to the Reactome Pathway Database.

source: Nine of the proteins were exclusively elevated in ABM and include proteins involved in inflammatory response (A2GL, HPT A1T1), fibrin clot formation (HEP2, PROS), LPS binding (CD14), and regulation of the complement cascade (CFAH).
